weekly_synthesis.text: This week's AI discussions reveal a strong emphasis on internalizing and tailoring artificial intelligence capabilities. Businesses are prioritizing strategic deployment and custom solution building, driven by a desire for greater control and maximized value

briefing_top_n.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
briefing_top_n.tldr: The release of sqlite-utils 4.0rc2 introduces significant improvements to transaction handling, ensuring that database writes are automatically committed upon method completion unless explicitly managed within a transaction. This version also refines the behavior of `db.query()` to execute and commit SQL immediately, resolving issues with uncommitted writes and incorrect transaction states. Additionally, it enhances error handling for invalid arguments and primary key management during upserts, and improves the `migrate` command's robustness.

briefing_top_n.title: Building a World Map with only 500 bytes
briefing_top_n.tldr: Iwo Kadziela, with assistance from Codex, has created a functional ASCII world map using only 445 bytes of data. The technique leverages deflate compression and a JavaScript snippet that utilizes fetch() with data URIs to decompress and display the map. This method allows for a surprisingly detailed map to be generated from a very small data footprint.

briefing_top_n.title: Better Models: Worse Tools
briefing_top_n.tldr: Newer, state-of-the-art Anthropic models like Claude Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 are reportedly worse at correctly calling external tools than older versions. Specifically, these advanced models sometimes invent extra fields in tool calls, causing rejection by systems like Pi. This suggests that recent training to improve tool use might inadvertently degrade performance on custom tools not part of their core training.

briefing_top_n.title: Free Fable 5 tokens this weekend? Here's how to max them
briefing_top_n.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefing_top_n.tldr: This article provides strategies for maximizing the use of Fable 5, an AI model, particularly during a free token weekend. It suggests that instead of using Fable 5 for general planning or coding, users should leverage it to design a "goal harness" that directs other coding models. The author also shares insights on integrating Fable 5 with tools like Blender, the effectiveness of short prompts for complex issues, and identifying suitable business problems for direct AI intervention.

briefing_top_n.title: Open Source AI Gap Map
briefing_top_n.tldr: Current AI, a non-profit initiative backed by significant funding, has launched the Open Source AI Gap Map v0.1. This map meticulously indexes 421 open-source AI products, including software, models, datasets, and hardware, categorized across the AI stack. The project also tracks an additional 24,400 artifacts and has released its underlying data under an MIT license on GitHub, making it explorable with tools like Datasette Lite.

cards.title: Every AI Agent Demo Stops at Email. I Pointed Mine at the Bills That Cost You Money.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: This article demonstrates how to build a single, reusable AI agent capable of handling complex and high-trust paperwork, such as insurance appeals and tax preparation, rather than creating a new agent for each task. The author explains that by mastering the pattern on low-stakes tasks like email management, one can then apply the same nine-step agent skeleton to more critical documents, ensuring human oversight remains in place for final decisions. This approach aims to make dealing with costly paperwork more efficient and affordable.

cards.title: Stop Wasting Money on the Wrong AI
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: This video provides a practical guide for choosing the right AI model for specific tasks to avoid overspending and confusion. It explains how to differentiate between daily-driver models and cheaper workhorse models like GLM 5.2, and when to utilize frontier models for uncertain jobs. The advice emphasizes routing familiar tasks to cost-effective models and keeping context portable to ensure workflow continuity as AI models evolve.

cards.title: Fable is back
cards.tldr: Fable 5 has returned for paid users, offering stronger guardrails and included in subscriptions until July 7th. It claims to handle 16% of remote work projects, double that of Opus 4.8. Additionally, Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5, which benchmarks similarly to Opus 4.8 on agent tasks but is more expensive in practice, and Gemini introduced two new media models: Nano Banana 2 Lite for fast, cheap image generation and Omni Flash for video generation and editing.

cards.title: I Built My Own AI Memory by Talking to Claude. It Did 80% Itself.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: You can now build approximately 80% of your personal AI memory stack by simply conversing with AI models like Claude or Codex. The key takeaway is that owning your AI's memory and intent is more crucial than renting the intelligence itself. This approach allows you to maintain control over your data and ensure agents only act with your explicit approval, with the build process becoming significantly less technical than before.

cards.title: The twilight of the chatbots
cards.tldr: AI models are rapidly improving in capability, with frontier models like Claude Fable and GPT-5.6 demonstrating the ability to complete complex software projects in hours that would take humans weeks. This acceleration is shifting AI usage from co-piloting with chatbots to assigning tasks to autonomous agents, even in non-technical fields. This rapid, exponential progress creates instability as human institutions struggle to keep pace with AI's accelerating capabilities.

cards.title: The AI Industry Is Losing
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: The AI industry is facing a potential bubble burst due to unsustainable capital expenditures by hyperscalers like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon. These companies are spending over a trillion dollars on AI-related infrastructure, outpacing their earnings and free cash flow, leading to significant debt accumulation. The author argues that the demand for AI compute, primarily from unprofitable companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, does not justify this massive investment, creating systemic risk for the tech supply chain, including semiconductor companies and cloud providers like Oracle and CoreWeave.

cards.title: Apple, Anthropic, And OpenAI Just Made The Same Move. Nobody Noticed.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The AI race is shifting from model intelligence to context control, with Apple, Anthropic, and OpenAI making moves to integrate AI into personal data and workflows. Apple is enhancing Siri with personal phone context, Anthropic's Claude Tag integrates AI into Slack, and OpenAI's Codex has gained trust for handling sensitive work. This move towards context-aware AI offers significant payoffs but also raises privacy concerns about data access.

cards.title: Fable's judgement
cards.tldr: The author learned from the Claude Code team that allowing AI models like Fable to use their own judgment, rather than strictly dictating their actions, can improve efficiency. This approach is particularly useful for tasks like deciding when to run tests or delegate coding to less powerful, more cost-effective sub-agents. By prompting Fable to use its judgment for these decisions, the author has found that their Fable token allowance is decreasing at a slower rate.

cards.title: June 2026 newsletter
cards.tldr: Simon Willison's June newsletter is now available to sponsors, featuring discussions on AI models like Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6, and GLM-5.2, which is noted as the new best open weights model. The newsletter also covers topics such as the decline of tokenmaxxing, updates on Datasette, sqlite-utils, shot-scraper, and miscellaneous WASM projects. It also includes a preview of the May newsletter for potential sponsors.

cards.title: llm-coding-agent 0.1a0
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has released llm-coding-agent 0.1a0, an experimental coding agent built on his "llm" agent framework. This new library, available on PyPI, leverages Claude code style and includes tools for file manipulation and command execution. Initial tests show promising results, with the agent capable of generating code for tasks like creating a SwiftUI CLI app, though it acknowledges limitations such as SwiftUI's unsuitability for true CLI development.

cards.title: Using DSPy to evaluate and improve Datasette Agent's SQL system prompts
cards.tldr: Simon Willison explored using DSPy to improve the system prompts for the Datasette Agent, which answers questions using SQL queries. By evaluating prompts with DSPy and testing against models like GPT 4.1 mini and nano, Willison identified a key area for improvement: including column names in the schema listing to prevent the agent from guessing column names and entering error loops.

cards.title: Understand to participate
cards.tldr: Geoffrey Litt argues that to effectively collaborate with increasingly sophisticated coding agents, developers must understand the code deeply enough to participate actively in the creative process. This understanding helps avoid cognitive debt and enables fluent, creative contributions. Litt's talk from AIE, which is available on YouTube and Twitter, emphasizes the importance of conceptual richness for meaningful participation in AI-assisted development.

cards.title: Quoting Anthropic
cards.tldr: Anthropic announced on June 30th, 2026, that the Department of Commerce has lifted export controls on their Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Access to these models will be restored starting the following day. This development signifies a change in regulatory status for Anthropic's AI offerings.

cards.title: I benchmarked the NEW Sonnet 5. The results shocked me.
cards.tldr: The author developed a repeatable benchmark, the How I AI Bench, to evaluate frontier AI models including the new Claude Sonnet 5. They tested Sonnet 5 against Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3 Pro across various tasks like PRD quality and agentic completion. The results, which combined human and AI scoring, were unexpected and led to specific model recommendations for different use cases.

cards.title: Nano Banana 2 Lite
cards.tldr: Google has released Nano Banana 2 Lite, also known as Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image, which is described as their fastest and cheapest Gemini image model designed for speed and scale. While it produced better results than previous Nano Banana models for a "Where's Waldo" style prompt, it did misspell "Forest Festival" in two different ways.

cards.title: What's new in Claude Sonnet 5
cards.tldr: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 5, which offers performance close to Opus 4.8 at a lower price point. While the base pricing remains the same as Sonnet 4.6, a new tokenizer effectively increases costs by about 30% for English and Spanish text, and 28% for Python code, due to a higher token count for the same input. The model features a 1 million token context window and has adaptive thinking enabled by default.

cards.title: The AI Compass
cards.tldr: A new interactive quiz called "The AI Compass" categorizes users into one of 30 AI ethics archetypes based on their answers to 29 questions. The quiz, implemented as a single-page React app using a Babel script tag, allows users to discover their AI persona. The author was personally categorized as "The Garage Tinkerer".

cards.title: Have your agent record video demos of its work with shot-scraper video
cards.tldr: The new shot-scraper video command, released in version 1.10, allows users to record video demonstrations of web application routines defined in a storyboard.yml file, utilizing Playwright for recording. This feature aims to enable coding agents to produce demos of their work, with the example provided showcasing the creation of new tables and data insertion in Datasette. The development of this feature was significantly aided by AI, with GPT-5.5 xhigh generating the code and documentation, and leveraging Playwright's improved screencast capabilities.

cards.title: shot-scraper 1.10
cards.tldr: Shot-scraper 1.10 has been released, introducing a new "video storyboard.yml" feature. This enhancement allows users to record video demos of websites directly using the command-line utility. The release focuses on improving the tool's capabilities for web scraping and creating video demonstrations.

cards.title: HTML table extractor
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has released a new tool that extracts HTML tables from pasted rich text, converting them into various formats like HTML, Markdown, CSV, TSV, or JSON. The tool has been updated to also import and display tables directly from Wikipedia pages using its CORS API. This builds upon his previous work on rich text conversion tools.

cards.title: Count the number of Safari tabs
cards.tldr: Simon Willison shared a tiny TIL on June 29th, 2026, demonstrating how to count the number of open Safari tabs using AppleScript. The command `osascript -e 'tell application "Safari" to count tabs of every window'` can be used to retrieve this information.

cards.title: Ornith-1.0: Self-Scaffolding LLMs for Agentic Coding
cards.tldr: DeepReinforce has released Ornith-1.0, a new family of open-weights LLMs built on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5, with variants up to 397B parameters. These models demonstrate state-of-the-art performance for their size on coding benchmarks and are capable of agentic tasks involving tool use. Initial impressions suggest proficiency in code navigation and generation, with good inference speeds.

cards.title: How Gusto’s CTO uses Claude Code to ship like a startup
cards.tldr: Gusto's CTO, Eddie Kim, led a team of five to build a new AI product, Gusto Cofounder, from scratch to launch in just 10 weeks by adopting a "no-process" approach. This involved using AI tools like Claude Code, implementing a "trash can" method for code reviews, and utilizing a "perma-Zoom" setup instead of traditional meetings. Notably, a designer with no engineering background achieved high productivity, and the team focused on an eval-first workflow for bug fixing.
